gaps.hint: noun needed after 'His'; note the -al suffix
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'refuse' is 'refusal' (-al noun); 'refuse' as a noun means rubbish.

gaps.sentence: We need ___ proof before we can act (CONCLUDE).
gaps.explanation: An adjective is needed before 'proof': conclusive (-ive). 'Conclusion' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: It was ___ of you to double-check the figures (SENSE).
gaps.explanation: 'It was sensible of you to do something' praises good judgement; 'sensitive' means easily affected.

gaps.sentence: The sky began to ___ as the storm approached (DARK).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -en forms the verb: darken means to become dark. A base verb follows 'to'.

gaps.sentence: Her answer was ___ , so we had to ask again (RELEVANT).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed — it did not relate to the question
gaps.explanation: The negative of 'relevant' is 'irrelevant' (ir- before r). An adjective is needed after 'was'.

gaps.sentence: He made a ___ mistake and lost all the data (CARE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: careless means not taking care. It modifies the noun 'mistake'.

gaps.sentence: The storm caused serious ___ (DESTROY) along the coast.
gaps.explanation: After the adjective 'serious' a noun is needed: destruction (-tion noun).

gaps.sentence: This grant will ___ her to study abroad (ABLE).
gaps.hint: positive verb needed: make it possible (en-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix en- forms the verb: enable means to make able. 'Disable' is the negative opposite.
